blueprint.title: Financial Ledger Aggregation Bug Hunt
blueprint.scenario: An internal C data pipeline reads raw transaction records from a SQLite database, applies a configurable aggregation engine, and writes daily rollup summaries back to a second SQLite table. The system has ~1200 lines across five C source files plus a runtime config file. An analyst noticed that per-category daily totals started disagreeing with the raw sums about three weeks ago, right after a 'harmless refactoring' was merged. The symptom looks like a rounding bug in the display formatter, but the real breakage is deeper.
blueprint.instruction_draft: Hey, something's wrong with the ledger pipeline in /app. I've been checking my daily category totals and they don't match the raw transactions in the database — the aggregated numbers are off. The pipeline reads from `ledger.db` (table `raw_txns`) and writes to `ledger.db` (table `daily_rollups`). Running `make && ./ledger_pipeline` should recompute everything. What I need: (1) each row in `daily_rollups` must have a `total_cents` equal to the exact integer sum of `amount_cents` for all raw_txns with matching `category` and `txn_date`; (2) each row's `tx_count` must equal the count of those matching raw transactions; (3) the `category` and `txn_date` values in `daily_rollups` must exactly match what's in the raw data — no dropped categories, no merged dates. Fix the pipeline code so this holds for any data loaded into `raw_txns`.
requirements: Each row in daily_rollups.total_cents equals the exact integer sum of raw_txns.amount_cents grouped by category and txn_date
Each row in daily_rollups.tx_count equals the count of matching raw_txns rows for that category and txn_date
Every (category, txn_date) pair present in raw_txns has a corresponding row in daily_rollups
No (category, txn_date) pair appears in daily_rollups that has no corresponding raw_txns rows
The pipeline must produce correct results for any valid data loaded into raw_txns, not just the pre-seeded sample
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm installs gcc, make, libsqlite3-dev, sqlite3, python3
Five C source files: main.c (~150 lines), db_reader.c (~200 lines), aggregator.c (~300 lines), formatter.c (~180 lines), db_writer.c (~200 lines), plus shared headers
A Makefile that builds the ledger_pipeline binary
A runtime config file /app/pipeline.conf with key=value pairs controlling behavior: AGGREGATION_BUCKET_SIZE, CATEGORY_HASH_SLOTS, DATE_GROUPING_MODE, OVERFLOW_STRATEGY
ledger.db pre-seeded with ~500 raw_txns rows across ~8 categories and ~30 dates, and a partially-correct daily_rollups table

Bug 1 (misleading symptom): formatter.c has an off-by-one in its display-only cents-to-dollars conversion that prints wrong values to stdout — this looks like the source of the mismatch but only affects display output, not the database writes

Bug 2 (real bug A): aggregator.c uses CATEGORY_HASH_SLOTS from pipeline.conf as the size of a fixed hash table for bucketing categories; the config value is set to 7 (a prime), but the hash function uses modulo against a hardcoded 8 (power of two leftover from pre-refactor), causing two categories to collide and their totals to be merged into one bucket, silently dropping one category's output and corrupting another's total

Bug 3 (real bug B): db_writer.c reads DATE_GROUPING_MODE from pipeline.conf; after the refactor the config key was renamed from DATE_GROUP_MODE to DATE_GROUPING_MODE but db_writer.c still reads the old key name, gets NULL, falls back to a default mode that truncates txn_date strings to YYYY-MM (dropping the day), causing all transactions in the same month to be merged into a single date bucket instead of per-day buckets

The two real bugs interact: fixing only the hash collision still produces wrong date grouping; fixing only the date grouping still produces wrong category totals; both must be fixed for cross-component consistency
A Python test harness /app/tests/verify.py that clears raw_txns, loads freshly generated transactions, runs the pipeline, and checks all three requirements against a reference computation
The pre-seeded sample data happens to have only one transaction per month per category in some categories, masking the date-grouping bug on casual inspection
blueprint.internal_hint: The solver must: (1) notice the formatter stdout discrepancy and investigate whether it affects the DB (it doesn't — red herring); (2) query daily_rollups vs raw_txns directly in sqlite3 to see actual numeric mismatches in the DB; (3) trace through aggregator.c and spot the hardcoded '% 8' vs the config CATEGORY_HASH_SLOTS=7, fix it to use the config value; (4) trace through db_writer.c and notice it calls config_get('DATE_GROUP_MODE') while pipeline.conf has DATE_GROUPING_MODE, fix the key name; (5) recompile and verify. The config file is the cross-component glue — it mediates between components that must agree on key names and on using the config value rather than hardcoded constants.
blueprint.trap: An agent that fixes only the formatter (the obvious symptom) sees the stdout output look correct on the pre-seeded sample and stops. An agent that finds and fixes only the hash collision bug passes roughly half the generated test cases (those with few categories or single-transaction months). Only fixing both bugs in aggregator.c and db_writer.c produces correct results across all freshly generated inputs, which include months with multiple dates and category counts that stress both hash slots and date grouping.
tests: Test 1 (basic correctness): Load 200 transactions across 6 categories and 10 distinct dates; run pipeline; for each (category, txn_date) pair assert daily_rollups.total_cents == SUM(amount_cents) and tx_count == COUNT(*) from raw_txns

Test 2 (hash slot stress): Load transactions designed so that with slots=7 and modulo-8 hashing, exactly two category names collide; verify both categories appear as separate rows in daily_rollups with correct independent totals

Test 3 (multi-date-per-month stress): Load transactions where the same category appears on 3 different days within the same calendar month; verify 3 separate daily_rollup rows exist for that category, not 1 merged row
Test 4 (zero-count guard): Verify no (category, txn_date) row appears in daily_rollups that has no corresponding raw_txns rows after a fresh load

Test 5 (coverage): Load transactions across all 8 categories used by the seeder, with at least 2 distinct dates per category; verify row count in daily_rollups equals the count of distinct (category, txn_date) pairs in raw_txns

Test 6 (large fuzz): Generate 2000 transactions with random amounts (1..9999999 cents), 12 categories, 60 dates across 3 months; run pipeline; compare every aggregated value against a Python reference computation using integer arithmetic

verifier_knob.name: num_generated_inputs
verifier_knob.effect: Lowering to 100 transactions / 4 categories / 5 dates reduces collision and date-grouping stress, making a partial fix appear to pass; raising to 5000 transactions / 20 categories / 90 dates increases the probability that both bugs manifest and interact in the same test run

expected_failure_modes: Agent fixes only the formatter display bug (the misleading symptom) and verifies against the pre-seeded sample, which looks correct in stdout
Agent finds the hash collision bug and fixes it but never investigates the date-grouping config key mismatch, passing tests with few dates per month but failing multi-date tests
Agent fixes the config key name mismatch but not the hardcoded modulo constant, passing date tests but failing category collision tests
Agent rewrites aggregation logic from scratch in a way that works for the sample but introduces an off-by-one or integer overflow for large generated amounts

Agent patches the config parsing to be case-insensitive or fuzzy-matching (masking the key name bug) but the hardcoded modulo remains, causing intermittent failures depending on generated category names

invalid_failure_risks: The hash collision bug depends on specific category name strings producing the same hash value under modulo-8 vs modulo-7; if the test harness generates random category names at verify time, the Test 2 'hash slot stress' test must use carefully chosen category names that are guaranteed to collide under the buggy modulo-8 scheme — if the harness uses purely random names, the collision may not occur and the test would not stress the bug as intended.

The pre-seeded daily_rollups table is described as 'partially correct'; if the pipeline appends rather than replaces rows, stale rows from the pre-seed could cause spurious failures in Test 4 (zero-count guard) or Test 5 (coverage) unless the pipeline or test harness explicitly clears the table before each run — the blueprint should specify this behavior.

Building five C source files with correct inter-file dependencies, a working Makefile, and a config parser that is intentionally broken in a subtle way is a non-trivial Docker image to construct correctly; if the image build has any latent compilation error or the config parser silently ignores unknown keys rather than returning NULL, Bug 3 may not manifest as described.

The large fuzz test (Test 6) with amounts up to 9,999,999 cents across 2,000 transactions could produce sums exceeding 32-bit integer range (~2 billion); if the C code uses int32 for accumulation, an agent who fixes the two described bugs but leaves an integer overflow in the accumulator would fail Test 6 for a reason not described in the bugs — this could be an invalid failure if the blueprint does not specify that the accumulator must be 64-bit.
review.reasons: The task is exceptionally well-designed: the three-layer deception (display red herring, hash collision, config key mismatch) creates genuine multi-step reasoning requirements, the fuzz-equivalence verifier makes hollow fixes impossible, and the interaction between the two real bugs ensures partial fixes fail deterministically. All five scores meet or exceed the threshold. The primary risks are implementation-level: the collision test requires pre-chosen category names rather than random ones, and the fuzz test's large amounts may expose an undescribed integer overflow bug that could cause invalid failures.
fixes: In Test 2, explicitly specify that the test harness uses hardcoded category names known to collide under modulo-8 (e.g., names whose hash values are congruent mod 8 but not mod 7), rather than relying on randomly generated names to happen to collide.

Specify that the pipeline unconditionally deletes all rows from daily_rollups before writing new results (or that the test harness does so), to prevent stale pre-seeded rows from causing spurious failures in Tests 4 and 5.

Explicitly state in the environment spec that amount_cents accumulation uses int64_t (or sqlite3's INTEGER which is 64-bit), so that Test 6's large-amount fuzz does not introduce an undescribed integer overflow bug that would cause an invalid failure mode not listed in the blueprint.

verdicts.reason: That task asks you to implement a MongoDB aggregation query in Python; this task asks you to debug a broken C pipeline writing to SQLite.

Both tasks involve fixing a broken financial data pipeline that writes incorrect aggregated totals to a SQLite ledger, with nearly identical correctness criteria (exact sums, counts, no dropped or spurious rows), differing mainly in language (Python vs C) and surface framing.
That task is about reading log files and generating a CSV metrics summary, with no debugging or database pipeline involved.
